clue.text: Swimming whales go to surface

definitions.note: an infinitive phrase meaning to get up out of bed

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving about and rearranging themselves

explanation.surface: Whales in the water head up to the surface to breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' looks like a description of the whales but is the anagram signal: WHALESGO rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The old naval call to rouse sleeping sailors became an idiom for getting up, which is what surfacing from sleep means.

clue.text: Warbles on one note — very monotonous

parts.note: warbles means sings in trills
G is one of the notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone sings on a single note, very dully.
explanation.definitionFit: A singsong voice rises and falls in a repetitive, droning way, extremely dull to the ear.

clue.text: Not in the pink or blue

explanation.surface: Not pink and not blue: a question of colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly unwell is the opposite of in the pink, and risqué jokes are both blue and of this kind.

clue.text: Fool swallowed up by crevasse

indicators.note: swallowed up says the word for fool takes the next word inside it

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool is swallowed by a crevasse.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a bottomless chasm, like a deep crack in a glacier.

clue.text: Write in large characters 'N144'

parts.note: the letter N is spelt out as en
a gross is twelve dozen, 144

explanation.surface: Instructions to write the code 'N144' in big letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter N spelt out is EN, and 144 is a gross.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross a document is to copy it out in large, formal handwriting.

clue.text: Small boat put into the water

explanation.surface: A dinghy is lowered into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is a small motor vessel, and to launch a ship is to set it afloat for the first time.

clue.text: Lion-tamer moves closer, and .

indicators.note: moves suggests the letters shift into new positions

explanation.surface: A lion tamer edges nearer to the beast, and the story continues in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOSERAND is rearranged; the clue runs on into 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fable Androcles pulled a thorn from a lion's paw and befriended it, taming the beast.

clue.text: … heads off nervous young lion, one lacking fibre

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their first letters
lacking means the word one goes without its final letter

parts.note: the clue word one, written out

explanation.surface: The story goes on: the tamer heads off a jumpy young lion that has lost a fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' takes the first letters of 'nervous young lion', and 'one lacking' is ONE cut short by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic material spun into thread, a man-made fibre.

clue.text: The village play

explanation.surface: The local village drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A small settlement is a hamlet, and Shakespeare's tragedy of the Danish prince has this title.

clue.text: Egyptologist to go over again, endlessly over

indicators.note: over signals that the shortened word is turned around
endlessly removes the last letter

parts.note: to retrace is to go over a route again

explanation.surface: An Egyptologist goes back over his old route, time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims RETRACE to RETRAC, and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Howard Carter was the archaeologist who discovered Tutankhamun's tomb in 1922.

clue.text: Application, if typed, to some extent showing style

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A job application that is typed looks smart and stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'style' is a noun, but the answer is an adjective, so 'showing style' is the definition. The run starts at the N ending 'Application' and continues through 'if typed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty is informal for smart or stylish, so something nifty is showing flair.

clue.text: Invest foreign currency in prestigious sporting achievement

annotationWithheld.why: Invest foreign currency in prestigious sporting achievement: RAND (foreign currency) gives the middle, but no reading of 'Invest' supplies G and SLAM around it
annotationWithheld.clue: Invest foreign currency in prestigious sporting achievement

clue.text: Sporadic pot-shots around rook cease abruptly

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters are placed about the next piece
sporadic means scattered and irregular, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Random shots fired at a rook suddenly stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporadic' rearranges POTSHOTS into STOPSHOT, and 'around' puts that about R for rook.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop short is an idiom for halting suddenly, which is ceasing without warning.

clue.text: Cat with quite a lot of scruples

explanation.surface: A cat with plenty of moral scruples.
explanation.walkthrough: A scruple is an old apothecaries' weight; twenty-four make this unit, so it is 'quite a lot of' them.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called by this name, and the unit is an old weight equal to many small scruples.

clue.text: Pasta for a starter in Naples — lots of it

indicators.note: a starter in a word is its opening letter, here taken from Naples

parts.note: oodles is informal for lots

explanation.surface: A diner in Naples orders a heap of pasta as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course, but it means the first letter, N, of Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are long strips of dough, a type of pasta.

clue.text: Fruit accompanied by only fish

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A meal of fruit served with nothing but fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This flatfish is a popular edible species.

clue.text: What makes a wave a wave?

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what turns a wave into a wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair curler creates a wave in the hair, and a long swelling breaker at sea also has this name.

clue.text: Develop — combines are able to

indicators.note: combines suggests the letters are mixed and joined together again

explanation.surface: A development plan: the merged firms are capable of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate an idea is to work it out in greater detail.

clue.text: He will remain outwardly nonchalant and determined

parts.note: contracted, he will becomes he'll
to be is to remain or exist

indicators.note: outwardly takes the outside letters of nonchalant

explanation.surface: A man stays cool on the outside while being fiercely resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' gives NT, the first and last letters of 'nonchalant'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bent on something with reckless resolve is to be set on it at any cost.

clue.text: In gym, tomboy performed quickly

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: PT is physical training, the school gym lesson
romp is an old word for a boisterous girl, a tomboy

explanation.surface: A tomboy shows off her speed in the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the British school gym lesson; romp as a word for a tomboy is old-fashioned and rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt describes something done without delay, so an action carried out swiftly.

clue.text: A warning — on account of that, one point is deducted

indicators.note: is deducted says the point is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: thereat is an old word for because of that
E is one point of the compass, east

explanation.surface: A caution: for that reason, one mark is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E (east, a compass point) from THEREAT gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace or intimidating statement serves to caution someone of trouble ahead.

clue.text: Conspirator who was envious of Norman falls

parts.note: Casca, one of Caesar's assassins, is 'the envious Casca' in Mark Antony's speech in Julius Caesar
de is the French, hence Norman, word for of

explanation.surface: A jealous plotter's view of a Norman.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony's line 'See what a rent the envious Casca made' fixes the conspirator; Norman French gives DE for 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, a series of falls of water.

clue.text: Twister going round on a bike

indicators.note: going round says the word for bike surrounds the other word

parts.note: a cycle is a bike

explanation.surface: Someone circles on a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a whirling storm, and a cyclone is a violent rotating storm.

clue.text: Arab staggering away from its borders

indicators.note: the border letters of the word, its first and last, are taken away

parts.note: lurching means staggering

explanation.surface: An Arab stumbles away from his country's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'street Arab' was an old term for a homeless child; 'away from its borders' drops the first and last letters of LURCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A street child or ragamuffin was once called a street Arab, so the two terms share a sense.

clue.text: State currency up in value.

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island
the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: A national currency has gained value.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has gone up in price is said to have climbed or increased.

clue.text: Establish a lead at tennis

explanation.surface: Building an advantage on the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something is to establish it, and a player one set ahead is said to be this.

clue.text: Musical sound from bird nesting right inside the hill

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend

indicators.note: inside puts the letter for right within the word for hill

parts.note: a knoll is a small hill

explanation.surface: A birdsong rings out from a bird nesting on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: The roc is the mythical giant bird of the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1950s pop style is a kind of music, here called a musical sound.

clue.text: A superior person, the French aristocrat

parts.note: nob is slang for a person of high social standing
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat thinks himself better than others.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble is a member of the peerage, a titled person of high rank.

clue.text: A tricky situation —.casserole starts to adhere to oven

parts.note: a hotpot is a casserole of meat with sliced potatoes on top, a Lancashire dish

indicators.note: starts of the following words means their first letters

explanation.surface: A cooking mishap: the stew begins sticking to the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotpot is a British stew topped with sliced potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an awkward issue nobody wants to handle, like something too hot to hold.

clue.text: Face can be a verb

parts.note: the word for a Native American warrior, usually a noun, can also be used as a verb meaning to face danger

explanation.definitionFit: To confront danger boldly is to face it, which is the verb sense of a word more often a noun or adjective.

clue.text: Kipper's head?

parts.note: a kipper here is someone who kips, and the slang word for a head also suggests one who dozes

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the head, and literally one who takes a nap, just as a kipper is one who kips.

clue.text: When holding strong chaps, surgeon has to be forcible

indicators.note: holding says the word for surgeon contains the word for the chaps

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
he-men are strong, macho men

explanation.surface: A surgeon must be firm when dealing with brawny patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means intense and forceful in feeling or expression.
